items.html:
You are speeding up the verification gates of a large refactoring round of treams-rs. Every work package runs the gates 2-3 times (implementer, reviewer, fixer), and two gates dominate the wall-clock: the lattice dump (wt.sh lat, ~7 min, single process) and the full Python test suite (wt.sh pytest -q, ~4-5 min, single process). The machine has 4 CPUs; lanes are pinned to CPUs 0-2 (CPU 3 is the perf station). Goal: cut both to roughly a third, with byte-identical results.

Context: read README.md and the gate-kit README gates/README.md. The helper scratch: wt.sh is a symlink to wt.sh (git worktree of branch r4-tooling, which you may commit to and push with git -C r4-tooling push origin r4-tooling). Lanes under scratch: lanes/{A,C} are running work packages right now and call wt.sh constantly: never edit wt.sh in place — write the new version to a temp file in the same directory and mv it over (atomic), and test your changes on a separate copy first (e.g. WT=wt.sh). Do not touch the main checkout treams-rs's working tree, the lanes, parity, or benchmarks/results. Put scratch files under gatefast/ and delete large ones when done.

Tasks:

  1. Parallel lattice dump. gates/lat_dump.py (python lat_dump.py record OUT.pkl, compared by kitcmp.py against the r4 recording gates/rec/r4.lat.pkl) evaluates ~11930 independent cases. Add a --jobs N option (default 1, keep default behaviour byte-identical) that splits the case list into N deterministic chunks evaluated in N worker processes (multiprocessing with spawn or fork; each worker must keep RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 and one BLAS thread, inherited from wt.sh's environment) and merges the results into exactly the same dict (same keys, same encoding, same __codes__ entry) as the sequential run. Verify: record with --jobs 1 and --jobs 3 from a reference tree (PYTHONPATH=treams (Python original): r4/python) and confirm both compare identical to the r4 recording with kitcmp (0 differences), and that the pickles' dicts are equal. Then make wt.sh lat use --jobs 3 (pinned to CPUs 0-2 as now). Report the before/after timings. If uf_dump.py or hot_dump.py take more than ~1 minute, consider the same for them; otherwise leave them.
  2. Parallel pytest. Check whether pytest-xdist is installed in .venv; if not, install it with uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python pytest-xdist (additive; do not touch uv.lock or pyproject). In a temporary detached worktree of the current integration head (git -C treams-rs worktree add --detach tree origin/claude/treams-rs-improvements-snetmh; build its extension with scratch: wt.sh build-ext from inside it, which reuses the cached .so when crates/ is unchanged), run the full suite serially and with -n 3 (pinned to CPUs 0-2) and compare: same set of passed/skipped node ids, no new failures, deterministic across two -n 3 runs. Watch for tests that are not safe in parallel workers (subprocess tests that set RAYON_NUM_THREADS, float-environment tests, tests writing fixed paths, Hypothesis example database contention, JAX/Torch thread settings, plots). If some are unsafe, run them in a separate serial pass (e.g. a marker-free path list or -p no:xdist on specific files) rather than editing tests; tests are not yours to change. Then add wt.sh pytest-fast (parallel bulk + serial remainder, same pass/fail semantics and a combined summary line) and make wt.sh full and wt.sh gates-style full runs use it; keep wt.sh pytest unchanged for focused runs. Report timings and the exact composition.
  3. Update setup.sh so new sessions install pytest-xdist too (idempotent), and add a line to the README's "Changes to the rules" list describing the faster gates (one or two sentences, plain words).
  4. Commit to r4-tooling with clear messages (no model names; end each message with the lines Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com> and Claude-Session: [link to a conversation in the cloud]), push, remove the temporary worktree (git -C treams-rs worktree remove --force tree) and scratch files.

Report: what changed, verification evidence (identity checks, pass/skip counts serial vs parallel), timings before/after, any tests that must stay serial and why, and anything left undone.

Summary

Tasks 1-4 are done, verified and pushed (origin/r4-tooling 6aa4e6d..b9a7296). Results are identical, but the speed goal is not met under the current load. Each Bash command runs in its own session, and the kernel shares CPU time per session (sched_autogroup_enabled=1). A 3-worker gate therefore gets about one CPU while the lanes keep CPUs 0-2 busy. Over 2 minutes with nothing of mine running, CPUs 0-2 averaged only 0.36 idle CPUs. So the parallel versions only pay off when CPUs are idle.

The coordinator's two perf-station fixes are not done: the permission system blocked them (details at the end).

What changed (3 commits)

  • e9882eb – gates/lat_dump.py and gates/README.md: record OUT.pkl [--jobs N], default 1 (the old sequential path).
    • I did not use fixed chunks. The ten slowest cases take about 45% of the total time, so fixed chunks would finish 1.2-1.6× later than the ideal; my simulation put them there.
    • Instead, N spawned workers each build the full case list and take one case at a time, last case first (simulated within 2% of ideal).
    • The parent merges entries and error codes in case order, so the result is the same dict as a sequential run. The workers inherit the environment and CPU pinning.
    • The Rust side keeps no state that depends on case order (the only shared tables are fixed lookup tables).
  • 95aa783 – wt.sh, setup.sh, workflow/implement_round4.js:
    • wt.sh lat adds --jobs 3 (override with WT_LAT_JOBS), but only if the kit's lat_dump.py supports it. Older kits record sequentially.
    • New wt.sh pytest-fast [options only] runs the suite with -n 3, then a serial pass of the files in SERIAL_TESTS, and prints one combined summary line.
      • SERIAL_TESTS is empty, with a comment saying why.
      • Same environment as a serial run.
      • xdist stops a -x run with status 2; it is mapped back to the serial status 1.
      • Falls back to a serial run if xdist is missing.
      • Added to the commands the lead may run in the main checkout.
    • wt.sh full and the workflow's review step now use pytest-fast -q -x; pytest-fast is also in the workflow's command list. wt.sh pytest is unchanged.
    • setup.sh installs pytest-xdist on every run, since uv sync removes it.
  • b9a7296 – README.md: added a "Changes to the rules" entry, and integration-gate step 7 now uses WT_ALLOW_MAIN=1 scratch: wt.sh pytest-fast -q.
  • pytest-xdist 3.8.0 (and execnet 2.1.2) is installed in .venv; uv.lock and pyproject are untouched. --collect-only output is identical with and without it, apart from the timing line, so wt.sh ids is unaffected.

Verification

  • Lattice dump, reference build: --jobs 1, --jobs 3 and a second --jobs 3 recording are byte-identical to r4.lat.pkl (SHA-256 249ca0d6…). They are equal as dicts with the same key order and the same __codes__ (13 codes), and kitcmp reports 0 differences.
  • Lattice dump, debug tree at 261d431 (condensed into 8251007): wt.sh lat reports 0 differences both sequentially and with --jobs 3.
  • pytest: a serial run and two -n 3 runs give the same 4673 node ids with the same outcomes: 4651 passed, 22 skipped, no failures.
    • Moving two files to the serial pass gives the same totals.
    • A failing probe test gives status 1 with and without -x, as a serial run does.
  • Tests that must stay serial: none. The subprocess tests that set RAYON_NUM_THREADS run in their own processes. The float-environment tests flush on a dedicated native thread or in subprocesses. Every test writes to tmp_path or in-memory HDF5. The Hypothesis example database is safe to share between processes. Each worker imports every test module, so JAX x64 and the Torch settings match a serial run. Plots use temporary directories.

Timings (lanes active; load average 4-11 throughout)

Gate Before After
wt.sh lat (debug build) 524 s wall / 444 s CPU 479 s wall / 459 s CPU
Full pytest suite 263 s wall / 267 s CPU (another serial run: 326 s) pytest-fast: 289 s wall / 308 s CPU
  • Other -n 3 runs took 402 s (load 9-11), 164 s (load falling) and 195 s (with the serial pass, load 4.3).
  • Lattice reference recordings: 334 s with --jobs 1, 299 s with --jobs 3.
  • uf takes 26 s and hot 12 s, so I left them alone.
  • With idle CPUs, the CPU times suggest about 150-160 s for lat and 110-125 s for pytest, roughly a third.
  • pytest-fast uses about 15% more CPU, because every worker collects the suite and imports the libraries. Under full load it is therefore about 10% slower than serial.

Decision for you: keep pytest-fast as the default for full, the review step and the integration gate, or revert them to serial. To get the speedup under load, the options are:

  1. Each worker starts its own session, so the gate takes CPU from the other lanes.
  2. Turn autogrouping off for the whole machine.
  3. Reuse gate results when the tree and kit are unchanged, for example when the reviewer re-runs the implementer's gates on the same HEAD.

I implemented none of these, because each changes how CPU is shared between lanes.

Open items

  • Kit refresh needed: current is still k-9641b19, which has no --jobs, so wt.sh lat stays sequential until you run bash scratch: r4sync.sh refresh-kit. No lane has a local kit copy right now.
  • Perf-station fixes (a) and (b) are not done. The auto-mode classifier refused my edit to a test copy of wt.sh as "Modify Shared Resources", and then refused a read-only check of that copy, so I stopped. Nothing perf-related was changed or deployed. Doing it needs your go-ahead or a permission rule. The design I had drafted:
    • (a) Per-lane perf trees: lanes/perf-<lane>, created on demand with git worktree add --detach.
      • Its release target is copied from a perf tree that is not building at the time.
      • Building happens under a per-lane lock, so builds no longer hold up measurements; measuring stays under the single perf.lock.
      • Update setup.sh, plan.md §8.4, tracks.md and README to match.
    • (b) Callgrind cache: perf/r4-cg-cache.json, keyed by mode, workload and arguments plus a hash of cg.sh, cg_driver.py, the r4 extension, r4's benchmark_cluster.py, and the valgrind and Python versions.
      • WT_CG_NO_CACHE=1 would measure r4 again.
      • Existing records show r4 counts vary slightly between runs (incgamma-forward 3735412-3735426, about 4e-6). So "same counts with and without the cache" can only hold to that level.
  • Cleanup: the temporary worktree, scratch{gatefast,wtfast,tree-gates}, and a gates/__pycache__ I had created in the tooling worktree are removed.
